text:
sam: quick share — I hit a perf regression after switching our quantizer to per-channel INT8 using the 'full' calibration set. profiler shows kernel selection flipped to a slower GEMM path for a subset of layers, KV cache hit ratio down ~12%, throughput -18%. attaching quick run.

sam: ```bash
./tools/profile.sh --model redwood-7b --quant int8 --calib-set ./data/calib/full.jsonl --seq 2048 --batch 4
# results (raw):
# throughput: 1500 tok/s
# p50: 14ms
# kernel: matmul_knl_v2 (fallback path)
```

marta: what's the "full" set composition — size, length distribution? any obvious outliers?

sam: full = ~10k examples (webtext + internal dev prompts). there are a few very long entries (some 4k tokens). suspect those long tails are skewing per-channel scale estimates, producing extreme scales and causing kernel pads/paths.

kei: per-channel is sensitive to outliers. have you tried percentile clipping on calibration activations (e.g., 99.9 / 99.95)? that usually stabilizes scales without moving to per-tensor.

anya: also try FP8 as a comparison — FP8 kernels pick a different compute path and sometimes run faster than int8 in our runtime. quality-wise it's different but worth perf baseline.

jordana: also check KV cache alignment — quantized matmuls changed the memory access pattern and we saw p50 spikes when cache hits fell. profiler trace should show increased L2 misses.

sam: ran a microbench: per-channel INT8 + percentile clip 99.5 -> throughput 1770 tok/s (-3% vs baseline), p50 12.1ms. quality delta small on our eval set. will post full numbers tomorrow.

ci-bot: perf-suite/job/1795000123 finished — summary: throughput 1826 tok/s (-3%), p50=12ms (+1ms), mem=13.2GB. artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/1795000123 :white_check_mark:

marta: proposal: automated calibration sampler that enforces caps — length cap (e.g., 1024) + drop top 0.1% by activation L2 magnitude. also add per-layer fallback table when scale variance > threshold.

kei: +1. add a kernel-flip trace in profiler so we can correlate exactly which layers flip to the slower kernel. include GEMM pad and microkernel id in traces.

anya: I can add a quick kurtosis and tail-mass metric to the quantizer to flag channels with heavy tails and force per-tensor for those channels.

sam: plan:
1) A/B test: full vs trimmed calib ds on int8 per-channel (I will run)
2) add kernel-flip trace to profiler (I will own)
3) run FP8 baseline for perf+quality (anya to take)

sam: @anya :thumbsup: ?

jordana: scheduled a 1hr slot Thursday to run the A/B and collect traces. will also run the KV cache microbench.

marta: quick governance question — should we default to percentile clipping at 99.9 for public builds or keep it opt-in?

kei: prefer 99.95 as default if perf matters, but 99.9 is a good conservative default for now.

sam: OK locking default to 99.9 and opening PR with config + perf numbers. will include per-layer opt-out table for layers that fail quality checks.

marta: thanks team. final ask: add a short eval prompt set that targets long-tail behavior so we don't miss regressions from clipping.

sam: noted — adding prompt set and PR link when ready. :eyes:
